design_rationale:
WHY THIS MAKES A GOOD TEST. The caller asks for one thing: the dental rider she posted a form to cancel
four days ago is still showing on her bill and she wants it actually ended, with whatever is left to
settle told to her. Everything else has to be found. Her rider premium account is missing a whole
quarterly billing cycle the plan never raised; her rider should have been suspended seven weeks ago and
never was, so the standing on the record is wrong and the figure it carries is the one a stale bill run
wrote; and when the closing figure is finally struck, two of the three coverage months just charged fall
beyond the day the rider ends and must come back to her, while a few dollars of her own money sitting
unapplied on the medical plan bill must be set against what is left. None of that is hinted at by the
caller, and none of it can be read off a single field: each figure is a multi-factor calculation over
the two ledgers and the two sets of published figures, the rider's and the medical plan's.

SCOPE TAKEN AND SCOPE LEFT. Task 0 occupied the two benefit claim subjects and two of the three rider
premium ledger subjects, with the tools settle_rider_benefit_line_e49937be,
reverse_rider_benefit_line_9daedfb7, pay_rider_premium_by_telephone_9597e982 and
post_rider_premium_credit_050a58f6. This task claims what was deliberately left: the third ledger
subject and the two rider lifecycle writes -- osb_ext_unbilled_cycle_premium_charge
(post_rider_premium_charge_4237e97e), osb_ext_unpaid_premium_suspension_arrears
(suspend_rider_for_unpaid_premium_a0d6b513) and osb_ext_rider_closure_settlement
(end_rider_at_member_request_09efad65). The two tasks' policy sets and tool sets are disjoint, and
between them they cover all seven extended policies of the difficulty. Nothing is reserved beyond them.

THE DRAW. scripts/draw_counts.py env/env_0006_medicare_advantage_plan_sponsor/tasks/optional_rider_benefit_desk --task 1
prints: {"task": 1, "key": "env_0006_medicare_advantage_plan_sponsor/optional_rider_benefit_desk/1",
"prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [5, 4, 5]}. The tree therefore carries
exactly two prerequisite problems besides the root, and the counts are taken as
osb_ext_unbilled_cycle_premium_charge 4, osb_ext_unpaid_premium_suspension_arrears 5,
osb_ext_rider_closure_settlement 5.

THE PROBLEM-TREE CARD.
  root  osb_ext_rider_closure_settlement -- end the rider at the member's own request and fix what is
        left owed on it.
  edge  osb_ext_rider_closure_settlement <- osb_ext_unpaid_premium_suspension_arrears, kind
        value_input, gate standing_basis, form state, resolved by
        suspend_rider_for_unpaid_premium_a0d6b513, owner agent. Prerequisite sentence: "The rider
        premium left owed when a rider is closed is fixed only once the rider stands suspended for
        unpaid premium on its own record." Four-point test: (1) the connective is "only once",
        affirmative direction; the negated contrapositive, "the rider premium left owed when a rider is
        closed is not fixed until the rider stands suspended for unpaid premium on its own record",
        carries the same result, the same waited-on state and the same scope, with nothing added,
        dropped or split; the affirmative direction was chosen because a figure a billing desk settles
        and quotes is stated as something it fixes once its grounds are in place, which is how the desk
        that strikes it would put it to a member. (2) The XX side is a record-visible state: the
        standing the rider record carries. (3) No tool, policy id or code token. (4) Exactly the edge's
        strength and scope. Exactly one write of this difficulty brings that state about: only
        suspend_rider_for_unpaid_premium_a0d6b513 sets a rider to premium_suspended;
        post_rider_premium_charge_4237e97e and post_rider_premium_credit_050a58f6 touch the balance
        alone, pay_rider_premium_by_telephone_9597e982 moves a rider the other way, to active, and
        end_rider_at_member_request_09efad65 sets terminated. Derivation: the sentence says the closing
        figure waits on the rider standing suspended; the record shows active; the suspension policy's
        own rule says what figure is struck when a rider is put into premium suspension, so that write
        is the one action that answers.
  edge  osb_ext_unpaid_premium_suspension_arrears <- osb_ext_unbilled_cycle_premium_charge, kind
        value_input, gate charges_counted, form state, resolved by post_rider_premium_charge_4237e97e,
        owner agent. Prerequisite sentence: "The rider premium standing owed is not struck until every
        billing cycle the rider has been in force through carries a rider premium charge on the rider
        premium account." Four-point test: (1) the connective is "until", negated direction; the
        affirmative contrapositive, "the rider premium standing owed is struck only once every billing
        cycle the rider has been in force through carries a rider premium charge on the rider premium
        account", is the exact equivalent; the negated direction was chosen because a figure the plan
        will not strike on an incomplete account is stated as a refusal to strike it. (2) The XX side is
        a record-visible state: whether each cycle carries a charge on the account. (3) No tool, policy
        id or code token. (4) Exactly the edge's scope. Exactly one write brings it about: only
        post_rider_premium_charge_4237e97e creates an osb_rider_premium_charge row. Derivation: the
        sentence says the figure waits on every cycle carrying a charge; the account shows charges for
        the March and June cycles only, while the rider has been in force since 2026-03-01; the charge
        policy's own rule says what rider premium is raised for coverage not yet billed, so that write
        is the one action that answers.
  Topological order: osb_ext_unbilled_cycle_premium_charge, osb_ext_unpaid_premium_suspension_arrears,
  osb_ext_rider_closure_settlement. The tree is a chain, so the order is unique; the argument and the
  two counterfactual runs are recorded in prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness, and each edge's seed
  evidence and deletion sensitivity in the same place.
  The customer's own write is the root: osb_ext_rider_closure_settlement is resolved by
  end_rider_at_member_request_09efad65, declared @tool(owner="user"), reached through
  unlock_user_discoverable_tool at action 11 and call_user_discoverable_tool at action 12. The base
  charter reserves cancelling a rider to the member -- "Only the member may cancel a rider they are
  paying for" -- and the act completes on the spot: the record is closed, the end date recorded and the
  figure left owed restated inside the same frozen clock.

THE BASE-INVARIANT CARD.
  Write osb_rider_premium_charge (osb_ext_unbilled_cycle_premium_charge). Governing base policy:
  osb_rider_premium_billing_and_posting. Gate rider_open_for_billing, kind state, authority
  system_record, correlation osb_riders.osb_rider_id bound to the action's osb_rider_id: the rider
  stands active, one of the three standings the gate allows. Gate payment_not_already_posted does not
  apply, its applies_to naming only osb_rider_premium_payment. No time gate on this subject.
  Write osb_premium_suspension (osb_ext_unpaid_premium_suspension_arrears). Governing base policy:
  osb_premium_suspension_and_recovery. Gate rider_grace_period_exhausted, kind time, correlation group
  osb_riders.osb_rider_id with osb_rider_premium_ledger.osb_rider_premium_entry_id, both bound to the
  action's arguments. The anchor is the day the plan posted the first unpaid rider premium charge,
  osb_rider_premium_ledger.posted_date = 2026-06-01; the duration is
  variants.rider_premium_grace_period_days = 60 for the Comprehensive Dental Rider; calendar days are
  counted from the day after that posting date, every day of the week counting, the last day of the
  grace period itself being inside it, so the grace period ran to 2026-07-31 and the premium has stood
  outstanding past it since 2026-08-01. Positive case: at 2026-07-31 the premium is not yet outstanding
  past the grace period and no suspension may be recorded. Negative case: at 2026-08-01 it is, and at
  the frozen clock of 2026-09-18 it has been for seven weeks. The whole temporal_basis is copied
  verbatim into solvability_contract.temporal_feasibility.
  Write osb_rider_termination (osb_ext_rider_closure_settlement). Governing base policy:
  osb_termination_and_cancellation. Gate cancellation_recorded, kind state, correlation
  osb_rider_requests.osb_rider_request_id bound to the action's osb_rider_request_id: intake c8227fef
  carries request_action rider_cancellation and intake_status recorded, both inside the gate's allowed
  set. The minimum holding months the tier requires are six, and the rider took effect on 2026-03-01
  with the cancellation received on 2026-09-14, so six whole months have passed and the rider may be
  cancelled; the cancellation rule the tier publishes is last_day_of_month_of_request, which produces
  2026-09-30. No time gate is declared on this subject in base.
  One base clause is superseded, declared clause by clause on
  osb_ext_unbilled_cycle_premium_charge: the sentence that rider premium is charged for each coverage
  month, because on a plan billed quarterly the rider premium is raised one billing cycle at a time
  rather than one coverage month at a time. Base's parameter values are untouched.

THE BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. The object of the call is one rider record, osb_riders row 556e787f, the
Comprehensive Dental Rider the member took out in February and has held since 2026-03-01; it is the only
rider she holds, so nothing else can be meant, and the correlation key is its own reference. The object
of the charge is the quarterly billing cycle beginning 2026-09, identified by the coverage month the
charge is booked to and correlated to the rider by its reference; the two cycles already charged are
distinguished from it by their own billing periods, 2026-03 and 2026-06. The object of the suspension is
the first rider premium charge that went unpaid, osb_rider_premium_ledger row f540db99 of 2026-06-01:
the charge of 2026-03-01 is excluded because the payment of 2026-03-08 settled it in full, and the
charge raised on this call is excluded because it is later. The object of the closing is the recorded
cancellation, osb_rider_requests row c8227fef, the only intake on the rider, which supplies both the day
the request reached the plan and the date the tier's cancellation rule produces from it. The two credits
of 2026-06-10 and 2026-07-05 each name the single charge they relieve, so neither can be mistaken for a
credit against any other.

WHY EACH CLASS OF SEED ROW EXISTS. The member profile carries the locating name and telephone number and
the two credentials the identity check is passed on. The medical plan enrollment c9b2d206 decides three
separate things: its standing in force and its quarterly billing frequency fix that one rider premium charge carries three
coverage months and that two of them fall beyond the end date; its published ninety days of grace, being
longer than the rider's sixty, fix the span the arrears figure is struck over; and its own premium ledger
carries the money left standing. Remove it and the charge falls from 85.80 to 28.60, the arrears figure from 73.40 to 85.80 and the closing figure loses the 4.80 USD set-off. The six medical plan premium
ledger rows give 433.20 USD paid against 428.40 USD charged: 4.80 USD left standing, deliberately less
than one month's rider premium so that it meets no coverage month when the cycle is charged but is still
set against the closing figure. The five rider premium ledger rows carry the settled first cycle, the
unpaid second cycle that put the rider past its grace period, and the two credits against it that the
credits ladder strikes only one of. The recorded cancellation intake is what the closing rests on and
what the months beyond the end date are counted from. The rider record's own balance of 46.40 USD is the
deliberate stale figure: it is what the last bill run wrote and is not what the entries give, which is
exactly the wrong answer an agent reaches who never finds the arrears-figure-basis factor. Automatic
clauses were checked: rider premium keeps running on a rider in arrears, which is why the September cycle
is owed; the rider has been held past its six minimum holding months, so the cancellation is permitted;
no benefit claim stands on the rider at all, the waiting period having ended only on 2026-09-01, so no
benefit maximum or frequency obligation is lit; and the medical plan enrollment stands active with
nothing owing, so nothing in another category is ignited.

THE PERSONA. Marguerite is seventy-five, unhurried and a little dry, ringing from her kitchen table with
a notice in front of her. She volunteers the surface goal in one breath -- she posted the form on the
fourteenth, nothing seems to have stopped, she wants it ended today and to be told what she still owes --
together with the hard preference that her health plan is not to be touched and that she will press the
button herself. Her name and telephone number come at once because they are how she is found; her date of
birth and Medicare number only when asked. Three things a representative would inevitably ask are written
out with their answers: what date she wants the cover to stop, which she cannot settle and refers back to
the plan; whether she has had any treatment, which she has not; and how the money leaves her account,
which she can only describe in general terms. Her reactions are tied to utterance events: she waits
patiently if told something must be put right first, she is surprised but not argumentative if told the
cover has already stopped paying, she performs the ending herself when it is handed to her with a date and
an amount, and she closes once she hears the rider has been ended and what is left to settle. She never
states a figure the policy computes and never corrects one.

THE DIFFICULTY, AND WHERE A CARELESS AGENT GOES WRONG. Four places bite. Reading the rider premium owed
off the record gives 46.40 USD and a closing figure of 78.80 instead of 11.40. Ending the rider without
first raising the unbilled cycle loses 85.80 USD of premium and strikes the arrears at nothing. Striking the arrears over the rider's own sixty days of grace rather than the ninety the medical
plan bill allows gives 85.80 instead of 73.40. And refunding at the amount of the charge rather than at
the rate the billing cycle divides it into wipes the closing figure to nothing. Each is excluded by the published rules alone.

THE STANDARD SOLUTION. Find the profile by name and telephone number, verify with the date of birth and
the Medicare number. Read the rider, its premium ledger, the recorded cancellation, the medical plan
enrollment and its premium ledger. Raise the quarterly rider premium of 85.80 USD for the cycle beginning
September that was never billed. Record the suspension that fell due on 2026-08-01, striking 73.40 USD.
Then tell the member the rider ends on 30 September 2026 with 11.40 USD left to settle, hand the ending
over to her, and let her make it.

THE VERIFICATION THAT WAS RUN. The three formulas were evaluated against the seeded world with the same
restricted evaluator the gate uses, each on the world as it stands at its own write step. The run prints:
  E: result=85.8  factor baselines 28.6 / 200.2 / 0.0 / 57.2         all-baseline 0.0
  G: result=73.4  factor baselines 85.8 / 245.0 / 0.0 / 55.0 / 132.2 all-baseline 132.2
  F: result=11.4  factor baselines 78.8 / 68.6 / 0.0 / 68.6 / 16.2  all-baseline 140.8
Every declared factor moves the number and every whole-baseline figure differs from gold. The prerequisite
sensitivity run prints G without the charge = 0.0 against 73.4, and F without the suspension = 78.8
against 11.4. Those are the figures recorded in computations and in prerequisite_closure.

THE DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT. With the extended yaml, the computations, the gold and
this dossier set aside, and working only from the rules as they will be published, the tool schemas, what
the share tools return on this seed and what the caller actually says, the same conclusion is reached: a
quarterly cycle is unbilled and must be raised at 85.80; the rider should have been suspended and the
figure struck over the ninety days the combined bill allows comes to 73.40; and the closing figure, after
refunding two months of the cycle just charged and setting off the money left standing on the plan bill,
is 11.40 with an end date of 30 September 2026. No second reading of the published text reaches a
different set.

REVISIONS. (1) Symptom: the arrears figure's governing-days-of-grace factor was decorative because the
charges, payments and credits ladders were all on tiers that ignored the window. Root cause: the selected
tiers took every entry on the account rather than the entries inside the window. Change: the tiers were
turned round so that a rider still in force strikes only what falls inside the days of grace that govern,
and the fall-throughs take everything. Re-run: the factor baseline gives 85.80 against a gold of 73.40.
(2) Symptom: the arrears-figure-basis factor decided `result` itself, which a factor may never do. Root
cause: the ladder was written onto the final binding. Change: the ladder moved to a binding of its own,
arrears_figure, with result rounding it, and a separate whole-account binding was added for the ended
tier so that the factor rests on records. Re-run: the structure gate passes and the figure is unchanged.
ROUND 2 - THE SOURCE-LAYER AUDIT. Two red lights bore on this task directly, and two charter-global
ones with it; each is closed here and none of the three scored figures moved.
(F3) Symptom: the arrears policy fixed the span in days of grace and the compute selected entries by a
whole-calendar-month window, so the set of entries struck was not the set the rule described; worse,
the tier whose stated value is "no days of grace at all" produced a one-month span, because the
conversion was floored at one. Root cause: a day count turned into a month count silently, and the
floor. Change: the rule now states the conversion it uses - the days that govern are reckoned into
whole months at thirty days to the month, any part month dropped, and the span runs back over that
many whole calendar months from the handling date - and says in the same breath that this bears on
which entries are counted and not on whether the days of grace have run out, which base counts in
calendar days and which this policy does not touch. The floor is gone, so no days of grace now yields
an empty span and no entry falls inside it, exactly as the tier says. The same construction in the
arrears-settlement policy of task 0 was fixed the same way. Re-run: 90 days still gives three months
and 60 still gives two, so every figure is unchanged, and the tier that could not be produced now can.
(F8) Symptom: cycle_months supplied both the refund rate and the months beyond the end date - 57.20 of
the 73.40 the closing figure is struck from - and no sentence of the closure policy's own rule said
how many coverage months a billing cycle carries; compute_basis covered the gap with the refund-rate
sentence, which fixes a different quantity. Change: the rule now carries the sentence in its own
voice, a billing cycle carries a single coverage month, three where the medical plan enrollment stands
in force and is billed quarterly, and the whole calendar months since the rider took effect where that
enrollment does not stand in force; compute_basis quotes it; and the branch that used to duplicate the
fall-through now states a different rule. The quantity is also declared as a factor of its own,
billing_cycle_length, rather than left as an anonymous ladder that moves the figure.
(F7) Symptom: refund_ceiling_basis declared cross_difficulty advantage and listed that difficulty's
bindings while the quantity it decided read no cross-category value at all. Change: the factor is
gone. The most that may be refunded is now plain plumbing - the charge carrying the most money on the
account, a credit never exceeding the charge it relieves, which is base's own rule - and the fifth
factor is billing_cycle_length, which genuinely reads the other product. The task's cross-difficulty
floor is now met by three factors that each make a real read.
(F2) Symptom: tier conditions naming "the rider is billed on the medical plan bill" divide no
customers, that parameter being True on all six variants; three ladders here lost a reachable tier and
one took the unreachable fall-through as its baseline. Change: that conjunct is gone from every ladder
in this task. The cycle-length, coverage-months-met, governing-grace and bill-money ladders now turn
on the medical plan enrollment's standing and billing frequency, on its published days of grace
against the rider's, and on whether its bill carries money received - all of which genuinely divide
customers. Re-run: gold unchanged; two factor baselines move, plan_bill_cycle_length from 0.00 to
28.60 and the replaced fifth factor to 68.60.
(F9) The rule said the months beyond the end date were those "of the billing cycle last charged" while
the compute read no charge row. Change: the sentence now says what the compute does - the coverage
months a billing cycle carries, less the month the cancellation reached the plan in and less any whole
calendar month passed since.
(O4, O5) Two observations are left as they stand. Recording a non-payment suspension on the way to a
voluntary cancellation is uncomfortable to read, but the suspension is independently due - the June
charge has stood unpaid since the grace period ran out on 2026-07-31 - and the plan cannot strike a
closing figure on a record it knows to be wrong; the sequence is a correction followed by the member's
own act, not a penalty. The 4.80 left on the combined bill buys no coverage month and is still set
against what is owed because those are two different questions, one asking whether the money covers a
whole month of cover and the other what is left to settle; each is fixed by its own sentence.

(3) Symptom: the closing figure came out at nothing. Root cause: the money left standing on the medical
plan bill was seeded larger than the figure it was set against. Change: the September payment on the plan
bill was reduced so that 4.80 USD stands over, below one month's rider premium. Re-run: the closing figure
is 11.40 and the months-met factor still bites on the charge.

ROUND 3 - THE RE-AUDIT OF THE ROUND-2 FIXES. revision_2 returned this task to SOURCE-POLICY RED on
R2-F2 alone, and carried four charter-wide items that bear on it. The diagnosis behind all of them
is one habit: a fix changed a rule sentence or a binding without carrying the change through to the
declarations that point at it. The full item-by-item answer is in 0.json's design_rationale; what
follows is what changed here. Nothing revision_2 marked PASS moved: the tree stands, all 14 factors
still bear weight against the same baselines, the unique solution is unchanged, the draw is
unchanged, the band (617 / MBI 6 / Tessier) is unchanged, and the three scored figures are still
85.80 with 2026-09, 73.40 and 11.40 with 2026-09-30.

  R2-F2, RED, closed. The two policies of this task that read a field of another category without
  declaring it were osb_ext_unbilled_cycle_premium_charge and osb_ext_rider_closure_settlement, both
  of which the F2 rework had taught to read advantage.status. "status" is now declared in each
  one's cross_category[0].reads. The one that mattered most is the closure policy: its
  billing_cycle_length ladder decides cycle_months, and through it refund_rate and
  months_after_end, and on this task that ladder carries 57.20 of a 73.40 basis, so it was resting
  on a field the policy did not admit to reading. I wrote a sweep that extracts the fields each
  compute actually reads across a category boundary and compares them with the declarations; it
  reproduced the re-audit's six problems before the fix and reports clean after it.

  R2-F4 (F12), one tool fixed, one explained. end_rider_at_member_request_09efad65 -- this task's
  user write -- now genuinely consumes osb_rider_request_id: it writes ctx.update
  ("osb_rider_requests", osb_rider_request_id, intake_status="completed", decision_date=today), so
  the cancellation intake Mme Tessier posted in on 2026-09-14 is closed out by the act that honours
  it. That is the right business effect, not a contrivance: an intake a plan has acted on does not
  stay open, and the base charter's own osb_rider_requests carries intake_status and decision_date
  for exactly that. Gold action 3's business_effect now states it, the docstring and the receipt
  state it, and REPLAY re-confirms determinism and that the closure still matches initial_state at
  15 tables. The intake is read as a base precondition before the write, in a status of recorded,
  awaiting_member_signature or under_review, and nothing computed downstream reads it, so no figure
  moves.

  suspend_rider_for_unpaid_premium_a0d6b513's osb_rider_premium_entry_id I am NOT claiming as
  fixed, and I do not want it recorded as one. It is still named in the receipt and written
  nowhere, and it cannot be made otherwise without editing frozen base. osb_riders carries no field
  able to hold a ledger reference -- its fields are osb_rider_id, customer_id, variant_name, status,
  linked_plan_reference, benefit_year, request_received_date, rider_effective_date,
  benefits_available_from, rider_end_date, waiting_period_basis, rider_premium_balance_due,
  annual_maximum_used, network_provider_reference and termination_reason -- and
  osb_rider_premium_ledger carries no field in which an entry can record that a suspension was
  struck against it. Nor can the parameter simply be dropped: base's rider_grace_period_exhausted
  evidence_contract names osb_rider_premium_ledger.osb_rider_premium_entry_id in its
  action_bindings, and check_solvability requires the tool signature to carry it. So the only
  non-cosmetic remedy is a new base field, which round 3 forbids. It remains a real thing the agent
  must get right -- the earliest unpaid charge is uniquely traced at evaluation_criteria[10] and is
  what the 73.40 is struck against -- but it remains inert in the DB, and the observation stands
  open against the base schema rather than against this difficulty.

  R2-F5 (F14), closed. All seven docstrings were re-scanned with an AST walk instead of by eye,
  which is why round 2's claim was wrong: the sed had missed every occurrence that fell across a
  line break. The scan now reports zero ordering words across all seven. Two of this task's tools
  were rewritten by it: "the first rider premium charge that went unpaid" became "the earliest",
  which picks out the same record without ordering anything, and "while the money stands owing"
  became "for as long as the money stands owing". The verbatim schema quote at
  evaluation_criteria[10].argument_uniqueness_tracing.osb_rider_premium_entry_id was swept and
  moved with it, so the tracing still quotes the docstring word for word.

  R2-O2, closed. osb_ext_rider_closure_settlement's cross_category note no longer speaks of a
  refund-ceiling factor that F7 deleted; it now says what that block's reads actually decide.

  R2-O5, accepted, no change. Both seeded enrollments are active, so the tiers F2 put on the "does
  not stand in force" side are reachable here but untaken. The remedy would be a third world, and
  the draw fixes this difficulty at two; reseeding either to exercise a fall-through would move
  figures the re-audit has already verified. Recorded rather than fixed.
user_scenario:
You are Marguerite Tessier, seventy-five, and you are ringing Ridgecrest member services from your kitchen table with a letter in front of you. Four days ago you posted back the form asking them to stop the dental rider you took out in the spring -- you have barely used it, the waiting period meant it paid for nothing at all until this month, and at your age you would rather have the money -- and this morning another notice has arrived telling you what the dental cover is costing. You open by saying you sent the form in on the fourteenth to end the dental cover and that you are ringing because it does not look as though anything has been stopped, and you would like it actually ended today and to be told what, if anything, you still owe on it so that you can settle up and hear no more about it. You are clear that you want the dental rider stopped and nothing else: your health plan is to carry on exactly as it is, and you say so plainly if there is any doubt. You will press the button yourself when the representative is ready to let you, because it is your cover and you would rather be the one to end it.

You give your name as Marguerite Tessier and the telephone number they have for you, 6175550937, when you are asked how to find you. If they ask for something more to prove who you are, you give your date of birth, 1951-06-30, and the number from your Medicare card, 6R48XT2PQ57, reading the letters out one at a time. If you are asked when you sent the form in, you say the fourteenth of September, that you posted it first class, and that you kept no copy. If you are asked what date you want the cover to stop, you say you assumed it stopped when they received the form and that you would rather they told you what the proper date is than have you guess. If you are asked whether you want the health plan touched, you say certainly not. If you are asked whether you have had any dental treatment at all under the rider, you say none whatever, not so much as a check-up, which is half the reason you are stopping it. If you are asked about the money that leaves your account each quarter you say it goes out by bank transfer, that you have never looked at it closely, and that they will know better than you what has and has not been taken.

You do not know the plan's own rules and you say so if pressed. You have no idea what is or is not sitting on your account, you have never been told anything was wrong with it, and you would not know one kind of charge from another. If the representative tells you that something on your record has to be put right before they can give you a figure, you say that is quite all right and you will wait; you are in no hurry and the kettle is on. prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree is a chain of three problems, each with a single out-edge, so it admits exactly one topological order: the charge, then the suspension, then the closing. There are no parallel prerequisites to reorder. The order is not left to convention either: each step's own rule states what its figure waits on, the suspension policy saying that the rider premium standing owed is not struck until every billing cycle the rider has been in force through carries a rider premium charge, and the closure policy saying that the rider premium left owed when a rider is closed is fixed only once the rider stands suspended for unpaid premium on its own record. Running the writes in any other order was tried and does not stand: with the suspension first, the figure struck is 0.00 rather than 73.40, because the cycle beginning in September carries no charge for it to strike; with the closing first, the standing basis is what the entries come to rather than the figure struck, and the closing figure is 78.80 rather than 11.40.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the charge changes the scored arrears figure from 73.40 to 0.00 USD, because the only rider premium charge inside the ninety days of grace that govern the span is the one this write raises. The charge row is also absent from the terminal state and osb_riders.rider_premium_balance_due never rises by 85.80.

Skipping the suspension changes the scored closing figure from 11.40 to 78.80 USD, because what stands owed is then taken as what the entries come to, 140.80 USD, rather than the 73.40 USD struck at suspension. The terminal rider record also never passes through premium_suspended and never carries the struck figure.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: The caller raises only the ending of her dental rider: she says she posted the form on the fourteenth, that nothing appears to have been stopped, and that she would like it ended today and to be told what is left to settle. She names neither prerequisite problem and nothing either of them resolves.
